true_positives.golden_comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Second downsize definition silently replaces the width/height overload and breaks its callers

This adds a second 'def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})' directly after the existing 'downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})'. In Ruby the later definition replaces the earlier one, so the width/height form no longer exists. Any caller passing five arguments now gets ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments). The diff also deletes the public 'OptimizedImage.dimensions(width, height)' helper and changes the positional signature of 'optimize'; any caller of those breaks too. Keep a single 'downsize' that accepts both forms, or update the existing callers and make the change explicit.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Client size limit hard-coded to 10 MB, ignoring the per-type site settings

The size check used to read Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']. It now uses a constant 10 MB for every upload type, so admin-configured limits for attachments and images are ignored in the browser. Users can attempt uploads the site was configured to reject, and the 'file too large' message reports 10240 KB even when the configured limit is lower. The 413 handler at line 246 has the same problem: it replaced the max_image_size_kb setting with the constant. The 'type' argument is no longer used for the size check at all.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

false_positives.candidate:
Animated-GIF detection depends on the tempfile path, so animated GIFs get flattened

The animated branch in optimize is chosen by matching the GIF extension against 'from', which is the request tempfile path. Rack multipart tempfiles are typically created without the original extension, so the check fails for uploaded GIFs even when allow_animated_thumbnails is enabled. downsize_instructions then uses '#{from}[0]', which keeps only the first frame. The result is that an oversized animated GIF is silently reduced to a still image on upload. Determine animation from the original filename or from the file contents, and pass that decision explicitly.

New downsizing behavior and changed limits have no tests, and the PR description is a placeholder

The PR adds a server-side loop that rewrites uploaded files, changes the public OptimizedImage downsize/optimize API, and replaces the download and client size limits with constants. No specs were added or updated. The description is just 'Test 1'. Nothing covers an image above the limit being reduced below it, the loop giving up after five attempts, a failed convert, the GIF branch, or the duplicate downsize signature (which a spec calling the width/height form would have caught).

Oversized images are uploaded anyway when downsizing fails or stalls

The loop calls OptimizedImage.downsize up to five times and ignores its return value. convert_with returns false (and swallows exceptions) on any failure, such as a missing binary, an unsupported format, or a corrupt file. After the loop there is no re-check of the size, so an image that is still above max_image_size_kb is passed to Upload.create_for as-is. The site's hard limit is therefore no longer enforced on the server. The input and output are also the same path, so a failed or partially written conversion overwrites the user's file with truncated data, and the next pass works on that damaged file. Check the result of each pass, stop on failure, and reject the upload if it is still over the limit.

Request-controlled 'type' ends up unquoted in a shell command via the tempfile name

For API URL uploads, the tempfile is created at line 55 with the name prefix 'discourse-upload-#{type}', where 'type' is the unvalidated params.require(:type) value. The new code passes tempfile.path to OptimizedImage.downsize, and convert_with (optimized_image.rb, around line 161) joins the instructions and runs them through backticks with the path unquoted. A 'type' containing shell metacharacters such as $(...), backticks, or ';' therefore becomes executed shell code. This is reached when an API caller uploads an image by URL that is larger than max_image_size_kb. It needs an API key, but it is still command execution that did not exist before this PR. Validate 'type', and pass arguments to the external process as an argv array (system, Open3) instead of a shell string.

Synchronous API uploads run up to five full convert and optimize passes in the request

For synchronous API uploads, the request thread now performs up to five ImageMagick conversions, each followed by ImageOptim.optimize_image! (which runs several external optimizers), on an image up to the 10 MB download cap, before responding. Each pass rewrites the whole file. A single pass with a scale factor computed from the size ratio, or moving the reduction into the deferred job, would avoid this cost.

URL download cap is now a fixed 10 MB, decoupled from max_image_size_kb

The download limit for API URL uploads changed from SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes to 10.megabytes. Two consequences. First, non-image files fetched by URL can now be up to 10 MB regardless of the admin's limit. Second, if an admin raises max_image_size_kb above 10 MB, images between 10 MB and the new limit are rejected at download time (the rescue nil turns the failure into a nil tempfile), which is the opposite of what the feature is meant to allow. Derive the download cap from the setting, or justify the constant.

true_positives.golden_comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
before_validation raises NoMethodError when host is nil

`self.host.sub!` is called before validations run. If host is nil (for example, the admin create or update request omits embeddable_host[host]), this raises NoMethodError instead of producing a validation error. The admin controller then returns a 500 rather than a 422. The format validator on line 2 would have rejected nil cleanly, but it never runs. Guard the nil case or add a presence check before normalizing.

true_positives.golden_comment: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
update and destroy crash with 500 for unknown ids

`update` and `destroy` use `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` without a nil check. For a nonexistent or already-deleted id, `host.host =` (line 23) or `host.destroy` (line 16) raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 instead of a 404. Use find (which raises RecordNotFound) or check for nil and return not_found.

true_positives.golden_comment: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
record_for_host does not downcase the input before comparing to lower(host)

The query is `lower(host) = ?` against the URI host, but the input is never downcased. Any mixed-case host fails to match a stored host. Callers include TopicRetriever#invalid_host?, which passes the raw embed_url param (only TopicEmbed normalizes URLs), so an embed_url with an uppercase host is treated as not embeddable and never retrieved. Downcase the host before the lookup.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Legacy host values are copied without normalization or SQL escaping

Values from the old embeddable_hosts setting are inserted verbatim. EmbeddableHost's before_validation strips the scheme and path, and the old allows_embeddable_host? accepted entries like 'https://example.com/1234' (it parsed them with URI). Migrated rows keep those prefixes, so EmbeddableHost.record_for_host, which compares lower(host) to a bare hostname, never matches them. Embeds for those sites silently stop working after upgrade. The value is also interpolated into SQL without escaping, so a host containing an apostrophe aborts the migration. Trailing '\r' from CRLF input is also kept. Normalize each entry (strip scheme, path, whitespace, and '\r') and use bound parameters.

true_positives.golden_comment: The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Fabricator definitions are swapped between the two files

category_fabricator.rb now defines :embeddable_host, and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb holds the :category, :diff_category, :happy_category, and :private_category fabricators. Fabrication loads every file, so specs still run. But the names are wrong: anyone looking for the category fabricators, or for the host fabricator, will open the wrong file, and the history of category_fabricator.rb is muddled. Swap the contents back so each file matches its name.

true_positives.golden_comment: The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Legacy host values are copied without normalization or SQL escaping

Values from the old embeddable_hosts setting are inserted verbatim. EmbeddableHost's before_validation strips the scheme and path, and the old allows_embeddable_host? accepted entries like 'https://example.com/1234' (it parsed them with URI). Migrated rows keep those prefixes, so EmbeddableHost.record_for_host, which compares lower(host) to a bare hostname, never matches them. Embeds for those sites silently stop working after upgrade. The value is also interpolated into SQL without escaping, so a host containing an apostrophe aborts the migration. Trailing '\r' from CRLF input is also kept. Normalize each entry (strip scheme, path, whitespace, and '\r') and use bound parameters.

true_positives.golden_comment: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migration aborts when no embed_category row matches, which is the common case

The category lookup `execute(...)[0]['id']` assumes at least one row. The query only matches when site_settings.embed_category holds the name of an existing category. Most installs never set that setting (its default is empty), so the result is empty, `[0]` is nil, and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError. The migration fails on upgrade. The intended fallback to the uncategorized category (`if category_id == 0`, line 14) can never run: it would need a matched row with id 0, and the crash happens first. The uncategorized lookup on line 15 also indexes `[0]['value']` without checking for rows.

false_positives.candidate:
Admin CRUD endpoints have no behavioral tests

The only spec asserts that the controller subclasses Admin::AdminController. Nothing covers create, update, or destroy; the category default to uncategorized (controller line 25); the response for an unknown id; validation failures; or the staff-only filter. embedding_controller_spec.rb has the same single inheritance assertion. A regression in the endpoints the admin UI depends on would pass CI. Add request specs for each action, including the failure paths.

Failed host deletion gives no feedback

delete() calls destroyRecord().then(...) with no catch. Every other request in this component uses popupAjaxError (see save on line 40). If the delete fails (for example a 403 or 500), the promise rejection is unhandled, the user sees nothing, and the row stays in the list. Add .catch(popupAjaxError).

Feed-imported topics lose their category, with no default left to configure

Previously every imported post was placed in SiteSetting.embed_category. That setting is removed here (site_settings.yml, server.en.yml, and the migration's DELETE). TopicEmbed.import now takes the category only from a matching EmbeddableHost. import is also reached from feed polling and import_remote, which do no host check. Feed-imported topics whose URL host is not registered silently land in the uncategorized category, and no admin setting remains to define a default. This is a behavior regression that should be called out or handled.

Host validation rejects TLDs longer than five letters

The regex requires the TLD to be `[a-z]{2,5}`. That rejects valid hosts such as example.technology, example.community, or example.international, and any host without a dotted TLD such as localhost. This is a new validator on a new table, so it blocks legitimate entries that the old free-text setting accepted.

Hosts saved with a port can never match

The format validator on line 2 explicitly allows an optional :port, and before_validation keeps it. But record_for_host compares against uri.host, which never includes a port. An entry like example.com:8080 is accepted by validation and can never match a referer or embed_url. Either reject ports in validation or compare host and port together.

No uniqueness validation or unique index on host

Nothing prevents two rows with the same host, case-insensitively or otherwise. The migration adds no unique index and the model has no validates_uniqueness_of. record_for_host (line 17) calls .first with no ORDER, so if duplicates exist with different categories, the category assigned to imported topics is arbitrary. Add a case-insensitive uniqueness validation and a unique index on lower(host).

PUT /admin/customize/embedding is a silent no-op

`update` renders the current embedding without reading params or saving anything, so the endpoint returns success while changing nothing. The client saveChanges action (admin-embedding controller) calls it with update({}), but the template has no save button, so the action is dead and the endpoint is misleading. Either implement the update or remove the route and the client action.

Test named for embeddable host checks behavior that no longer exists

expandable_first_post? no longer reads embeddable hosts, so the test 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' passes only because the built topic has no TopicEmbed row (has_topic_embed? is false for an unsaved topic). It does not exercise host presence at all, and no test replaces the old 'hosts disabled' coverage. The nested describe on the following lines is also misspelled ('emeddable').

_ids sideloading yields undefined entries and throws on null

_hydrateEmbedded now maps every *_ids array through _lookupSubType. If the referenced collection is absent from the payload, _lookupSubType returns undefined for each id, and the result is an array of undefined entries. The `hydrated || []` fallback on line 200 never applies because map always returns an array, so the undefined entries survive. The embedding template then renders a row per entry. Separately, `obj[k].map` throws when the _ids value is null. Previously *_ids keys were ignored entirely, so a single null field now breaks hydration of the whole record. Filter out missing entries and guard null before mapping.

category_id is never checked against an existing category

`belongs_to :category` does not verify that category_id points to a real category, and the table has no foreign key. The admin controller passes through any integer (app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb line 24). Deleting a category, or saving a bad id, leaves a host pointing at nothing. TopicEmbed.import then passes that id to PostCreator, so new embed topics get a dangling category. Validate that the category exists.

find embedded test changed to id 2, but the fixture always returns fruit 1

The test now calls store.find('fruit', 2), but the /fruits/:id pretender route in create-pretender always returns fruits[0] (apple, id 1), ignoring the id. The assertions therefore check apple's colors. Changing the id suggests coverage of the banana record (color_ids [3]) that does not exist. Either make the fixture honor the id or revert the id to 1.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Nil TopicUser dereference when no membership row exists

`TopicUser.find_by` can return nil (for example if the row was never created or was removed), and `tu.notification_level` is then called without a guard, which raises NoMethodError and returns a 500. Using `TopicUser.change`, which creates the row when it is missing, would avoid this and also fix the persistence problem noted for the save! call.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')

false_positives.candidate:
New unsubscribe action has no specs

Nothing covers the new action: the logged-out redirect, the 301 slug redirect that must happen before any state change, the notification_level transitions (tracking or watching to regular, regular to muted), or a missing TopicUser row. The message_builder_spec change only passes an extra argument and does not assert that the link appears in the body or HTML. A spec that re-reads the topic_user row after unsubscribe would have caught the auto-track persistence bug.

Route name and template path do not match, so the unsubscribe template may never render

The route is declared as a top-level `this.route('topicUnsubscribe', ...)`. Ember derives the default template name from the route name (topicUnsubscribe, or topic-unsubscribe), not from the path topic/unsubscribe, so the new templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs is likely not the template used for this route. The page could render blank or fall back to the application template. Either rename the template to match the route or nest the route under the topic resource as this.route('unsubscribe'). I have not verified the resolver behavior in the running app.

State-changing unsubscribe is exposed on GET with no CSRF protection

The action mutates notification_level, but it is reachable via GET (config/routes.rb: `get 't/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe'` and `get 't/:topic_id/unsubscribe'`). Rails' forgery protection does not cover GET, so any page that embeds the URL (for example an img tag on another site) will mute a logged-in user's topic. Mail link scanners and prefetchers will also trigger the mutation without the user clicking. A state change like this should be a POST (with a GET confirmation page), or should use a signed token like the existing email/unsubscribe/:key flow.

Unrelated summary route constraint silently removed

The diff rewrites the summary routes and drops `post_number: /<digits>/` from their constraints (both `t/:slug/:topic_id/summary` and `t/:topic_id/summary`). The unsubscribe feature has nothing to do with summary URLs, and the change is not mentioned. Either revert it or explain why it is safe, since the constraint's effect on a route with no post_number segment is not obvious.

Unsubscribe only steps watching/tracking down to regular, contradicting the email text

The email copy says 'You will stop receiving notifications for <title>', but for users at tracking or watching the action sets notification_level to regular. Regular still sends notifications for replies and mentions, so those users keep getting notified. Only users already at regular are muted. Either mute for every level or change the wording.

Unsubscribe writes notification_level directly, so auto-tracking can silently undo it

`tu.save!` changes notification_level without going through `TopicUser.change`. `TopicUser.change` also sets `notifications_reason_id` (user_changed) and `notifications_changed_at`, and publishes the change on MessageBus. Here the reason stays NULL for any topic whose level the user never explicitly set. `TopicUser.update_last_read` (the CASE expression in topic_user.rb) and `TopicUser.auto_track` both switch a topic to tracking when `notifications_reason_id IS NULL` and the user's viewing time passes the auto-track threshold. So after a user clicks the unsubscribe link and the topic is muted, the next read can flip it back to tracking, and the promise in the email to stop notifications is silently broken. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic.id, notification_level: ...)` instead.

add_unsubscribe_link now requires unsubscribe_url or email building raises

The unsubscribe_link string now interpolates %{unsubscribe_url}. html_part (line 67) and body (line 90) call I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args), and template_args only contains unsubscribe_url if the caller passed it. Any caller that sets add_unsubscribe_link: true without unsubscribe_url, including plugins that use this public builder, will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument while building the email. Either default the URL in the builder or render the topic line only when the URL is present.

track_visit! uses the topic id as the user id when given an integer user id

`user_id = user.is_a?(User) ? user.id : topic` falls back to `topic`, which is the topic id, instead of `user`. TopicsController calls `TopicUser.track_visit! topic_id, user_id` with integer ids, so `user_id` becomes the topic id. The update then hits (or creates) the topic_users row for whichever user has the same id as the topic, and the real user's last_visited_at is never recorded. This predates the PR, but the PR edits this same method (line 125), so the fix belongs in this change.

true_positives.golden_comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Validation side effect increments match_count on every valid? call, so one signup counts twice

should_block? writes to the database (match_count += 1, last_match_at, save) and it runs inside the User email validator. Every valid? call counts as a match. UsersController#create calls user.valid? (line 168) and then user.save (line 172), which runs validations again, so one blocked signup attempt increments match_count by 2 and the statistics the spec describes as 'whether those emails have ever been blocked' are inflated. Any other valid? call, such as a form or preview check, also counts. The counter should be incremented once per blocked attempt (for example in the controller or a dedicated check), not as a side effect of validation.

true_positives.golden_comment: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Domain whitelist/blacklist regex is unanchored, so it matches addresses where the domain is only a substring

Regexp.new("@(#{domains})", true) matches the domain anywhere after an '@'. With a whitelist containing gmail.com, an address like x@gmail.com.attacker.net satisfies the check and passes, which defeats the whitelist. With a blacklist containing spamclub.com, a@spamclub.com.example.org is also rejected. This logic was moved here verbatim from User, but this PR rewrites it into a new validator and it is a security control, so the pattern should be anchored to the end of the address (for example matching '@domain' followed by end of string, case-insensitively).

true_positives.golden_comment: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Blocklist lookup is case-sensitive, so changing the case of an address bypasses it

should_block? does BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first with no normalization, and EmailValidator passes the raw submitted value. A blocked entry 'bad@spamclub.com' does not match 'Bad@spamclub.com', and the unique index on blocked_emails.email is also case-sensitive, so rows differing only by case can coexist and .first picks one arbitrarily. Anyone blocked can register again by changing the case of any letter. The codebase already has Email.downcase (used in users_controller#change_email and User.find_by_username_or_email), so both the stored value and the lookup should be normalized the same way.

false_positives.candidate:
Any server email error marks the address as rejected and then shows a generic 'is invalid' reason

The new branch adds result.values.email to rejectedEmails for any result.errors.email, including 'has already been taken' and 'is not allowed from that email provider'. emailValidation then returns the fixed reason I18n 'user.email.invalid' (lines 69-73) for that address, so the field says 'is invalid' even when the address is valid and was rejected for another reason. The flash message shows the server reason, but the field and the form state contradict it, which is misleading to the user.

Validator spec stubs the blocklist, so no test exercises the real blocking path or the moved domain rules

Both examples stub BlockedEmail.should_block?, so the table, the case-sensitivity behavior, and the match_count side effect are never exercised here. Nothing verifies that a User with a blocked address fails validation, that a case variant is blocked, or that the whitelist/blacklist branches, which this file now owns, still behave as before. The double-counting issue would also go unnoticed. Add a spec that creates a BlockedEmail record and checks User validity end to end, including a case variant and a count-after-valid? expectation.

match_count is updated with a non-atomic read-modify-write

record.match_count += 1 followed by record.save reads the current value and writes back the incremented one. Two concurrent signups for the same blocked address can both read N and both write N+1, losing an increment. Use an atomic update (for example BlockedEmail.update_counters(record.id, match_count: 1) or a SQL increment) together with the last_match_at update.

true_positives.golden_comment: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Origin check uses substring match, so look-alike origins are accepted

discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1 checks whether the sender origin is a substring of discourseUrl, not whether it equals it. If discourseUrl is 'https://forum.example.com/', a page at 'https://forum.example.co' passes the check and can send 'discourse-resize' messages. The impact is limited to setting the iframe height, but this is the only origin validation in the embed script and it is wrong. The comparison should parse discourseUrl and compare origins for equality.

true_positives.golden_comment: The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Article URL interpolated unescaped into stored HTML footer

The URL is placed unescaped into an href attribute and a text node of the footer, which is then stored as raw HTML. The only check is that the URL starts with http(s):// (line 11). Characters such as single quote, equals and parentheses are legal in URL paths and can pass URI parsing, so a feed link like http://example.com/'onmouseover='alert(1) produces an anchor with an injected event handler. The URL should be HTML-escaped before interpolation.

true_positives.golden_comment: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
'<%- end if %>' is a syntax error; the best view cannot render

The block opened on line 2 is closed with 'end if', which is not valid ERB/Ruby for closing a conditional. It compiles to 'end if ;', where the modifier 'if' has no condition, so the template raises SyntaxError whenever it is rendered. Every request for an existing embedded topic (the @topic_view branch) fails. It should be '<%- end %>'.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
One bad feed item aborts the whole poll; nil content is not guarded

The loop has no per-item rescue. If any item raises (for example i.content is nil, which is possible for entries with only a summary, so nil.scrub raises; or TopicEmbed.import raises on a PostCreator or permission error), the remaining items are never imported. The job is also scheduled with retry: false, so the failure is dropped until the next hourly run hits the same item again.

true_positives.golden_comment: The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
ALLOWALL is not a valid X-Frame-Options value

The only valid values are DENY, SAMEORIGIN and ALLOW-FROM. Browsers ignore unrecognized values, so this line only appears to allow framing by accident, and it overwrites any app-wide frame policy with a meaningless string. To allow framing, the header should be removed (for example response.headers.delete('X-Frame-Options')), not set to an invalid value.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

false_positives.candidate:
--category option removed with no replacement and no documentation

The method_option :category and its only use are deleted. Existing invocations that pass --category or -c now fail with an unknown-option error. The import also changes behaviour: the topic is now built by scraping the article with readability (TopicEmbed.import_remote) instead of a permalink post, and created_at is no longer set on the topic. The PR description is only 'Test 4', so none of this is documented.

A retrieve job is enqueued on every request; the throttle only runs inside the job

When no topic exists, every request enqueues a retrieve_topic job, and the 60-second throttle is checked only when the job runs (topic_retriever.rb:27-28). Anonymous requests, and the loading page that reloads every 30 seconds, therefore create unbounded queue entries even when the URL was retrieved moments ago. The throttle check should happen before enqueueing, or duplicate jobs should be deduplicated.

Adding a NOT NULL column with a default rewrites the posts table under lock

On PostgreSQL releases before 11, add_column with default: 1 and null: false rewrites the entire posts table while holding an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock. On a large forum this blocks all reads and writes to posts for the duration. The safer pattern is to add the column nullable, backfill in batches, then set the default and NOT NULL constraint.

CGI.unescapeHTML turns escaped feed markup into live HTML

RSS and Atom descriptions are almost always entity-escaped (a script tag appears as <script>). After CGI.unescapeHTML those entities become real markup. The result is saved with cook_method raw_html (topic_embed.rb:22) and rendered unescaped (see post.rb:133 and embed/best.html.erb:19), so any feed item can inject script into the forum for all visitors. Escaped content should stay escaped, or be sanitized, never unescaped.

Gate tests pass for the wrong reason; poll_feed itself is untested

feed_polling_enabled defaults to false (site_settings.yml). The 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' examples never enable feed_polling_enabled, so execute returns early at the first gate and the expectation holds regardless of the gate under test. Only the 'delegates' example enables all three, and it mocks poll_feed. The actual import loop, nil handling and failure behaviour have no coverage.

PostCreator enqueues jobs inside an open transaction

PostCreator.create is called inside the outer Topic.transaction (line 21). PostCreator.create calls enqueue_jobs before returning, which queues process_post and feature_topic_users. Its own comment (post_creator.rb around line 290) says jobs must be enqueued after commit. With Sidekiq, a worker can start before this transaction commits and find no post, so the job silently does nothing. The TopicEmbed row is also created after those jobs are queued.

Protocol-relative URLs are rewritten to a wrong absolute URL

An href like //cdn.example.com/a.png starts with '/', so the sub(/^\/+/, '') strips both slashes and the result is prefix + '/cdn.example.com/a.png', i.e. http://host/cdn.example.com/a.png. The same problem exists for img src (line 71). Protocol-relative links should keep their host, or be resolved with URI.join against the article URL.

Shipped migration now uses force: true, which drops an existing table

This changes an existing migration to create_table with force: true. If top_topics already exists with data in any environment where the migration version is not recorded (for example a database built from another branch), this migration drops the table and all its rows without warning. The flag is not needed for a table this migration is supposed to create for the first time and should be removed.

Spec asserts raw HTML is stored and rendered verbatim

The assertion post.cooked.should == post.raw locks in the behaviour that imported content is stored as-is with no sanitization. Nothing tests escaping of the article URL in the footer, sanitization of feed or scraped HTML, the unchanged-content update path, or import_remote. The security-relevant paths of this feature are not covered.

Test name says 404 but asserts only non-success; referer mismatch is untested

The example 'is 404 without an embed_url' does not set a host, so it fails on the host check and never exercises the missing-parameter path. It only asserts not-success, so it does not verify a 404. There is also no example for a referer whose host differs from embeddable_host, which is the main access check in ensure_embeddable.

URL validation uses ^ instead of \A, so it matches any line

In Ruby, ^ matches at the start of any line. A value such as 'javascript:alert(1)' followed by a newline and 'http://x' passes this check. The later URI() call in absolutize_urls currently rejects it, so no harm follows, but the validation is ineffective and relies on an unrelated exception. The regex should be anchored with \A.

Unauthenticated requests can trigger a full feed download and reimport each time

The throttle is keyed on the full embed_url (lines 26-28). Only the host must match embeddable_host, so a client can vary the path or query string to get a fresh key every time. Each new key then calls Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute here, which downloads the entire feed and re-imports every item (poll_feed.rb:29, 31-36). The feed fetch and the readability fetch (topic_embed.rb:48) use open() with no timeout. An attacker can therefore keep Sidekiq workers busy with unbounded outbound fetches and DB writes. The feed poll needs its own global throttle or should not run inline per URL.

raw_html posts are stored and rendered without any sanitization

When cook_method is raw_html, cook returns the raw text unchanged, skipping the markdown pipeline, any sanitizer and the after_post_cook plugin filters. Imported content (RSS items via PollFeed, scraped pages via TopicEmbed.import_remote) is stored this way (topic_embed.rb:22), and PostCreator accepts cook_method from any caller's options with no whitelist (post_creator.rb:216). The cooked value is then emitted unescaped: embed/best.html.erb:19 uses 'raw post.cooked', and normal topic views render cooked as HTML. Any markup that reaches a raw_html post, such as a script tag in a feed item, runs as stored XSS on the forum's own origin for every visitor. Remote HTML needs sanitizing before it is stored as cooked.

setnx and expire are not atomic; a crash leaves the throttle key without a TTL

The key is set with setnx and then given a 60-second expiry in a separate command. If the process dies between the two, the key never expires and that embed URL is throttled permanently for non-staff users. A single atomic SET with NX and EX options would avoid this.

false_positives.candidate:
Fallback chain is rebuilt and SiteSetting is read on every backend lookup

Fallbacks#translate in the i18n gem calls `I18n.fallbacks[locale]` on every backend translate, including the interpolated translations that bypass the LRU cache (`args.length > 0`). Each call reads `SiteSetting.default_locale`, calls `to_sym`, and allocates a new array with `uniq.compact`. This is a small per-translation cost on a hot path. Computing the chain once per locale, or caching it in the hash, would avoid it.

Fallback locales are only loaded by the controller filter, not by I18n.t

The translate override loads only `config.locale` (`load_locale(config.locale)`). The fallback chain's other locales (the site default and :en) are loaded only by `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!`, which is called from `ApplicationController#set_locale`. Any translation made under `I18n.with_locale` outside a web request (Sidekiq jobs, mailers rendered in jobs, rake tasks) therefore has no guarantee that the fallback yml files are loaded. If the key is missing in the requested locale, the lookup falls back to a locale whose translations were never loaded and returns a 'translation missing' string. The fallback behavior depends on which entry point ran first, which is fragile.

Loading fallback locales does not invalidate the LRU translation cache

The cache at line 71 is keyed only on key, locale, and backend object_id, and is cleared only in `reload!`. Results now depend on which fallback locales are loaded and on `SiteSetting.default_locale`, but neither is in the key. If a lookup runs before the fallback locale (e.g. :en) has been loaded, the 'translation missing' result is frozen into `@cache`. When `ensure_loaded!` later loads :en, that stale entry is still served for that locale until the process restarts. The same staleness applies when an admin changes `default_locale`, since cached fallback output for other locales is not recomputed.

No specs for the new fallback chain, ensure_loaded!, or the set_locale change

This PR changes locale resolution for the whole application: it adds a custom fallback order (user locale, site default, :en), a new `ensure_loaded!` path in the I18n accelerator, a new call in `set_locale`, and it removes `config.i18n.fallbacks` from three environment files. None of this is covered by a spec. Nothing checks that a missing key falls back in the expected order, that fallback locales get loaded, or that the behavior holds in production and profile environments after the config removal. Given the cache and loading issues above, targeted specs are needed before merge.

true_positives.golden_comment: The OptimizedCursorPaginator in organization_auditlogs.py attempts to use negative slice offsets on Django querysets, but Django querysets do not support negative slicing and will raise an AssertionError.

Django QuerySet does not support negative indexing and raises ('Negative indexing is not supported'), so any cursor with a negative offset produces a 500. The cursor comes from the client-supplied query string, so an admin can trigger this by crafting a cursor. The comments at lines 876 and 878-879 say Django 'properly handles negative slicing automatically' and that this grants access 'beyond normal pagination bounds'; both claims are false, and the advertised behavior never works.

true_positives.golden_comment: get_item_key assumes a numeric key, but the paginator is used with order_by=-datetime in the audit logs endpoint; calling math.floor/ceil on a datetime will raise a TypeError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:

get_item_key copies the numeric logic from Paginator: `value = getattr(item, self.key)` followed by `math.floor(value)` / `math.ceil(value)`. The endpoint sorts by `-datetime`, so self.key is 'datetime' and the value is a datetime.datetime. math.floor(datetime) raises TypeError. build_cursor calls this key on the first result whenever a page has any rows (via _build_next_values), so with `?optimized_pagination=true` from a superuser or global-access user, every non-empty audit log page returns a 500. DateTimePaginator avoids this by converting to a millisecond timestamp. value_from_cursor here also returns the raw cursor integer, which build_queryset would compare against a datetime column even if the key function worked. The optimized path is unusable as written.

false_negatives.golden_comment: When requests are authenticated with API keys or org auth tokens (which have user_id=None), organization_context.member is None. Importing non-existent OptimizedCursorPaginator

false_positives.candidate:
Advanced pagination gated on bare User.is_superuser instead of an active superuser session

Sentry gates superuser behavior on an active superuser session (is_active_superuser(request)), so this bypasses the session-level elevation check. It also introduces a new authorization decision (superuser or global-access member unlocks a different paginator and negative-offset handling) outside the endpoint's permission class, controlled by a client-supplied `optimized_pagination` query parameter.

The only change in Cursor.__init__ is a comment saying it 'allows negative offsets' and 'enables efficient reverse pagination'. The code (`self.offset = int(offset)`) is unchanged and already accepted negative values before this PR. Rejection of negative offsets happens in the paginators, so the comment describes a behavior that does not come from this line and misleads readers about where the behavior lives.

New pagination path and gating logic have no tests and the PR description is empty

The PR adds a new paginator class, a new query-parameter switch, a superuser/global-access gate, and changes to the shared BasePaginator offset handling, but adds no tests. The description is just 'Test 1'. A single test requesting `optimized_pagination=true` with a non-empty audit log would have exposed the datetime TypeError in OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key. Tests should also cover negative cursor offsets, permission gating for non-admin members, and the unchanged default DateTimePaginator behavior.

The comments describe the optimized path as 'high-performance' and 'efficient browsing of large audit datasets'. For non-negative offsets the optimized path issues the same queryset, ordering and slice as DateTimePaginator, and it adds no index, query or caching change. The only behavioral difference is the negative-offset path, which crashes. The comments and the PR title overstate what the change does.

Shared BasePaginator silently clamps negative next-page offsets, leaving cursor arithmetic inconsistent

For next-page cursors, the query now starts at max(0, offset), but build_cursor still receives the raw negative cursor.offset. When the key value is unchanged, _build_next_values computes next_offset = offset + limit from the negative value. The returned page therefore starts at row 0 while the next cursor is computed as if it started at a negative position, so consecutive pages can overlap. Before this change such cursors raised an error; now they return wrong pages silently. BasePaginator is shared by DateTimePaginator, Paginator and every other endpoint using them, so this changes behavior well beyond the audit log endpoint. The change is also not a performance optimization, and no tests cover it.

true_positives.golden_comment: OptimizedCursorPaginator's negative-offset branch in get_result() passes cursor.offset directly as start_offset to queryset slicing when enable_advanced_features is True and cursor.offset < 0.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Negative cursor offset is passed to queryset slicing, which Django rejects with a 500

In OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result, when enable_advanced_features is set and cursor.offset is negative, start_offset is passed unchanged to queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django QuerySet does not support negative indexing and raises ValueError ('Negative indexing is not supported'). An admin who sends optimized_pagination=true with a negative cursor offset gets an unhandled 500. The comments at lines 874-880 claim the ORM 'handles negative slicing automatically' and that this exposes data 'beyond normal pagination bounds'; neither is true. The class also copies BasePaginator.get_result (line 821 onward) almost line for line, so the two implementations will drift.

true_positives.golden_comment: In BasePaginator.get_result(), when cursor.is_prev is True, it sets start_offset = offset without clamping, allowing negative offset values to be passed to queryset slicing.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Forward-cursor offset clamp changes BasePaginator behavior for all paginated endpoints

BasePaginator.get_result is shared by DateTimePaginator and Paginator, which many endpoints use. The new line clamps negative offsets to 0 for forward cursors. Previously a negative offset made queryset slicing raise. Now it silently returns the first page. The same negative offset on a prev cursor still passes through unchanged and still raises, so the behavior is inconsistent. The comment on lines 179-181 says negative offsets are 'allowed' for bidirectional paging, but forward pages now do the opposite. No tests cover this change, and it is not gated behind the new optimized path.

true_positives.golden_comment: Accessing .has_global_access on organization_context.member can raise an AttributeError when organization_context is None, particularly for non-superuser non-member users.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
organization_context.member is dereferenced without a None check

RpcUserOrganizationContext.member is Optional. For a non-superuser, the expression organization_context.member.has_global_access raises AttributeError if there is no membership record. Whether this is reachable depends on OrganizationAuditPermission admitting non-members, which this diff does not show. Guard with a None check, or confirm the permission guarantees membership.

false_negatives.golden_comment: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key uses floor/ceil on a datetime key (order_by='-datetime'), causing TypeError.

false_positives.candidate:
Comment claims a capability that this change does not implement

The added comment says it is a 'performance optimization' that allows negative offsets for 'efficient reverse pagination from arbitrary positions'. The only change is this comment: int(offset) was already unvalidated. Downstream, forward pages clamp negatives to 0 and prev pages pass them into queryset slicing, which raises. The comment advertises behavior that does not exist and will mislead future readers.

Module docstring still describes span-buf:s:* keys as sets

The glossary says span-buf:s:* keys are 'the actual set keys', and the flow above says payloads are added to 'the set'. After this change these keys are sorted sets scored by end_timestamp_precise, which is what the eviction and flush logic depends on. The docs should say so.

New optimized_pagination branch and its admin gating have no tests

The branch that switches to OptimizedCursorPaginator with enable_advanced_features=True, the superuser/global-access gate, and the fallback to DateTimePaginator are all untested. The negative-offset path that 500s for admins (paginator.py line 882) would be caught by even a single endpoint test. Add tests for the admin path, the non-admin fallback, and a negative cursor.

The loop bound changed from 10000 to 1000 and the comment that documented the limit was deleted. The change is unrelated to span eviction and is not mentioned in the PR. Redirect chains deeper than 1000 now stop early, leaving set_span_id at an intermediate span, so later spans are attached to the wrong segment with no error or metric. Restore the original bound or justify the change explicitly.

Segment key type changed from SET to ZSET without migration, so in-flight keys break on deploy

The per-segment key type changes from a Redis SET to a sorted set: sadd becomes zadd here, sscan becomes zscan in _load_segment_data, and sunionstore becomes zunionstore in add-buffer.lua. The key names (span-buf:s:{...}) are unchanged and segment keys live for up to redis_ttl (3600s). During a rolling deploy, or for up to an hour after, old-version SET keys still exist. New code then hits WRONGTYPE on zadd, on zcard/zunionstore/zpopmin inside the Lua script, and on zscan in the flusher. redis-py pipelines raise on command errors, so process_spans fails for any batch touching a legacy key, and flush_segments can fail for every segment in the same batch. That stalls ingestion and flushing until the old keys expire. The fix needs a new key prefix or explicit handling of the type mismatch.

Span eviction at 1000 is silent: no metric or log, and it replaces an observable limit

When a segment exceeds 1000 spans, zpopmin silently deletes the lowest-scored (earliest-ending) entries. The buffer.py change also removes the old flush-time guard, which logged an error and emitted spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded. Segments that used to be dropped and logged are now silently truncated, and operators have no signal that spans are being discarded. Add a counter or log for the number of evicted spans.

Tests do not cover eviction, score ordering, or the set-to-zset change

The PR's purpose is eviction above 1000 spans, but no test inserts more than 1000 spans or checks which spans survive. Every fixture uses the same constant end_timestamp_precise=1700000000.0, so score-based ordering is never exercised. The zunionstore SUM collision is also untested, as is the old-SET-key compatibility problem. Add a test that inserts more than 1000 spans with distinct end timestamps and checks that the latest 1000 survive, plus a case where the same payload arrives twice.

Unrelated audit-log, paginator, and cursor changes are bundled into a spans-buffer PR with a placeholder description

The PR title describes a spans buffer optimization, and the description is only 'Test 2'. The diff also changes the audit-log endpoint, adds an experimental pagination class to api/paginator.py, and changes utils/cursors.py. Nothing in the description explains why these belong together or how they are meant to behave. Split them into separate PRs with descriptions, or document the intent.

max_segment_spans is now a dead parameter; the eviction limit is hard-coded to 1000 in Lua

SpansBuffer still accepts max_segment_spans (default 1001), but nothing reads it. Its only use, the span-count check in _load_segment_data, was removed. The real limit is the hard-coded 1000 in add-buffer.lua line 62. Callers tuning this parameter get no effect, and the two limits disagree. Either pass the limit to the script through ARGV or remove the parameter.

zunionstore uses default SUM aggregation, corrupting scores of members present in both sets

ZUNIONSTORE without an AGGREGATE option sums scores. When a member (same payload) already exists in set_key and is also in the source key, for example a redelivered span, its score becomes the sum of two end timestamps (about 3.4e9) instead of end_timestamp_precise. zpopmin uses these scores to choose which spans to evict, so eviction order is corrupted. The same problem applies at line 53 for the parent key. Use AGGREGATE MAX or MIN so scores remain timestamps.

true_positives.golden_comment: The upsampling eligibility check passes the outer dataset instead of the actual dataset used by scoped_dataset. In paths where the query ultimately runs against discover (e.g., dashboard split) while the original dataset is metrics, upsampling may be skipped even when all projects are allowlisted.

Upsampling decision uses the request's dataset instead of the dataset the call runs against

The dashboard split path calls _get_event_stats with `discover` for errors_only_query and transactions_only_query, and with split_dataset elsewhere. When the request dataset is `errors`, _should_apply_sample_weight_transform returns True, so the transactions-only discover query also gets count() rewritten to upsampled_count(). Bare except swallows errors and the helper changes every store_event call

_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling wraps both the lookup and the float conversion in bare 'except Exception: pass'. A malformed contexts value is silently dropped, and the test sees no sample rate with no signal. The helper is invoked unconditionally from store_event (line 1049), so it affects every test that stores an event, not just the upsampling tests. Comments claim caching and consistency that the code does not provide

The comments say 'this cached result ensures consistent behavior across query execution' and describe a performance optimization. Nothing is cached in this function. The eligibility is recomputed on every _get_event_stats call, which can be up to four times per request in the split path. The transform is also applied in three separate places (lines 232-233, 276-277, 295-296). The comments mislead the next maintainer about what is cached and why.

Docstrings contradict each other and the performance rationale is unsupported

The function docstring (lines 23-25) says the 60 second cache avoids expensive repeated option lookups. The NOTE in _are_all_projects_error_upsampled (lines 50-53) says the allowlist is read fresh on every call and that this is intentional. The cache at lines 30-38 contradicts the second claim. The performance rationale is asserted without measurement, and the cache adds its own round trip on every request.

Endpoint tests skip topEvents, dashboard split, and mixed-row queries

The new class covers only plain count() timeseries for an error query, an all-allowlisted and a partial-allowlist case, and a transaction-only query. Not covered: topEvents with upsampling (the top_events_timeseries branch rewrites columns too), the dashboardWidgetId split path (where the dataset-scope bug lives), dataset=errors routing, and queries that mix error and transaction rows. test_error_upsampling_with_transaction_events checks only a transaction-only query, which never reaches the rewrite, so it does not exercise the case the gate exists to block. The upsampled_count aggregate is also not tested directly.

Equations and orderby still use the unweighted count()

The rewrite is applied only to the timeseries columns. Equations from get_equation_list (line 256 in the top-events branch, and in the RPC branch) and the orderby still refer to raw count(). A request mixing count() with an equation over count() returns a weighted count column next to an unweighted equation, which is inconsistent within one response.

Error-focus gate is a substring match on the raw request query

`"event.type:error" in query` is True for `!event.type:error` (exclude errors) and for `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`. In both cases `count()` is rewritten to `upsampled_count()` (sum of sample_weight) even though transaction rows are in scope and carry no sample weight, so counts come out wrong or the query fails. The gate also reads `request.GET['query']` (line 135) rather than the query string that actually executes. The split paths in organization_events_stats.py append `AND !event.type:transaction` or `AND event.type:transaction` to the query, so the gate's decision and the executed query can disagree.

Gate tests miss the negated and OR cases the substring check gets wrong

The discover gate is tested only with a plain 'event.type:error' query and a plain 'event.type:transaction' query. It is not tested with '!event.type:error', with 'event.type:error OR event.type:transaction', or with the split-path query shapes. Those are exactly the inputs where the substring check gives the wrong answer, so the bug above would pass this suite.

Reads an option that this change does not register

options.get('issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist', []) is called here, but the diff does not register this key in sentry/options defaults. Sentry's options manager raises for unregistered keys. This call runs on every cache miss for any events-stats timeseries request, before the dataset check. If the option is not registered elsewhere, those requests fail. The endpoint and unit tests mock sentry.api.helpers.error_upsampling.options, so they cannot catch this. Confirm the registration exists or add it.

Rewritten column uses an alias suffix that the field grammar does not accept

The rewrite produces the literal string 'upsampled_count() as count'. Sentry's field grammar takes function(args) with nothing after the closing paren, so this string will not match the function form and will be treated as an unknown field or fail to parse. That turns affected requests into errors. The upsampled_count aggregate is only registered in DiscoverDatasetConfig (discover.py), yet _should_apply_sample_weight_transform also enables the rewrite for the `errors` dataset. Nothing in the diff shows this resolves through the errors query builder.

Stray submodule-pointer file committed to the repository

The PR adds a file named 'sentry-repo' whose only content is 'Subproject commit a5d29095...'. This looks like a submodule pointer written as a plain file, with no .gitmodules entry. It adds a meaningless file to the tree and looks like a leftover from a local submodule operation. It should be dropped from the PR.

Unrelated change to a public API error message

The topEvents validation message changes from 'If topEvents needs to be at least 1' to 'topEvents needs to be at least 1'. This is a wording change to a public API response that the PR description does not mention and that no test update in this diff accompanies. Clients or tests matching the old string will break.

invalidate_upsampling_cache is dead code and the 60s staleness is unmitigated

invalidate_upsampling_cache is defined but nothing in this change calls it. The eligibility cache set at line 38 has a 60 second TTL and is keyed only by org and project set. Removing a project from the allowlist therefore keeps upsampling it for up to a minute. The docstring says the function 'should be called when the allowlist configuration changes', but no call site exists.

sum(sample_weight) silently undercounts events that have no weight

The docstring says the schema guarantees sample_weight for all events in allowlisted projects, so no null checks are needed. Nothing enforces that: the allowlist is per project, not per event. An event whose SDK does not send contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate may have a NULL or zero sample_weight. sum() skips NULLs, so such events contribute 0 instead of 1 to the count, silently, in any allowlisted project with mixed traffic.

toInt64 truncates a float sum and can undercount by one

sample_weight is a non-integer float (1/sample_rate), and toInt64 truncates toward zero. A float sum that lands just below an integer, for example 9.9999999999, becomes 9. Round before casting, e.g. round(sum(...)), so the integer result is not systematically low.

upsampled_count is a public aggregate with no allowlist gate

The new aggregate is registered without private=True, unlike the adjacent function in the same converter. Any discover or events query can therefore call upsampled_count() on any project. The allowlist check exists only in the count() rewrite, so users can request an upsampled value for non-allowlisted projects, where sample_weight is typically absent and the result is 0 or misleading. The component guards only on isError and tooFewFeedbacks. useFeedbackSummary types summary as string | null and returns data.summary unchanged. New None max_segment_id branch has no test that exercises it

The early return for max_segment_id is None is not reached by any test. test_delete_replays_bulk.py changes a fixture row to None, but it mocks delete_matched_rows, so _make_recording_filenames never sees that row. Nothing asserts that a None max_segment_id yields no filenames instead of failing on range(None + 1).

Org saved-search conversion migrations gutted; referenced replacement migration is not in the PR

The conversion body of 0920 (and of 0917) is replaced with an early return. The comment points to 0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py, which is not among the changed files, so no migration in this PR converts org-level SavedSearch rows into GroupSearchView. Org saved searches will silently never become views for any environment where this lands. The 0917 migration test is also deleted. Either include the replacement migration and its test, or do not remove the conversion logic here.

get_environment_info calls issue.get_recommended_event() for every issue (up to five per PR) while building the comment, which loads a full event per issue inside the PR-comment task. The only output is an environment name. This adds per-issue I/O on every comment refresh. Consider using environment data already available or caching it.

Typo 'the the' in story text

The Getting Started story reads 'Below is the the most basic example of the table'. The duplicated word should be removed.

A title containing '**](https://evil.example) **' closes the link text early and injects an arbitrary link into the bot comment posted on a PR. The title (and the environment name placed in backticks) should be escaped before formatting.

Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

false_positives.candidate:
Assertion is vacuous: expect(promise).toBeTruthy() always passes

`isChecked()` returns a Promise, so `expect(page.locator(...).isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` checks that a Promise object is truthy and always succeeds. The FIXME above it acknowledges this. The PR edits this block but keeps the vacuous check, so the enable test does not verify the switch state. Use `await expect(page.locator(...)).toBeChecked()`.

The codes are shown only in the DisplayBackupCodes step, which is reached after the enable endpoint has already set twoFactorEnabled=true. The Dialog still receives `onOpenChange`, so Escape, an overlay click, or the X button closes the modal without calling `onEnable` or the 'Close' button. Toggling it again then fails in setup with TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled. If the authenticator is later lost, the user has no recovery path. The step should ignore dismissal (or require an explicit acknowledgement), and the dismissal path should still notify the parent.

Copy button reports success without awaiting the clipboard write

No tests exercise backup-code login, backup-code disable, or single-use consumption

The new server logic (backup-code branch in authorize, backup-code branch in disable.ts, code consumption, MissingBackupCodes/IncorrectBackupCode errors) has no test coverage. The PR checklist says no tests were added, and the only addition is a TODO. The enable/disable e2e flow only checks the download, copy, and close buttons. true_positives.matched_candidate:

This line passes that wrapper directly to prisma.credential.update as `key`. With sync disabled (the default), every Google access-token refresh (about hourly) overwrites the stored key with `{ success: true, data: {...} }`, which has no top-level access_token, refresh_token or expiry_date. In the sync branch the helper returns the fetch Response without reading the body or checking response.ok. true_positives.golden_comment: The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

refreshAccessToken receives `credentialId` (the Cal.com credential primary key) and passes it as the third `userId` argument to refreshOAuthTokens. Every other provider passes credential.userId. With CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT enabled, the self-hoster endpoint is asked to refresh tokens for calcomUserId equal to a credential id, which is a different user. The returned tokens are then written into this user's credential, mixing accounts. The fix is to pass the user id (credential.userId) and keep the credential id only for the DB update.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Salesforce now refreshes its token on every client construction and bypasses the sync endpoint

getClient runs from the constructor (line 57) and now always POSTs to login.salesforce.com and writes the credential row, even when the stored token is still valid. Every availability check, booking or list call that creates a service instance pays a network round trip and a DB write, and concurrent instances race on the same refresh token. Because this bypasses refreshOAuthTokens, Salesforce still calls Salesforce directly in sync mode, which defeats the PR's purpose. The statusText !== 'OK' check on line 86 is also unreliable (HTTP/2 responses have an empty statusText) and should check response.ok. Finally, the minimal schema applied to this direct response strips instance_url, so the stored key loses it when sync is enabled.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.
true_positives.matched_candidate:

appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body) throws a ZodError on a bad body, and JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) (lines 57-59) throws on a wrong key or non-JSON plaintext. Neither is caught, so the caller gets an unstructured 500 rather than a 400 with a stable message. Use safeParse for a 400 response and wrap decryption and parsing in a try/catch.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

false_positives.candidate:
In sync mode the HubSpot refresh writes a fetch Response object into the credential key

In sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, so hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn is undefined and expiryDate (line 192) becomes NaN. Line 198 then persists that Response object as the credential key. A Response has no token fields, so the stored key ends up with no access or refresh token (at most an expiryDate of null). If Prisma rejects the object instead, the refresh fails silently in the catch. Either way the HubSpot connection is never refreshed and its stored tokens are lost. The sync body must be parsed to JSON and the expiry derived before anything is persisted.

The PR checklist states that no tests were added. The new endpoint (secret check, decryption, create/update logic) and the shared helpers (refreshOAuthTokens, parseRefreshTokenResponse) have no unit tests. Defects in this PR, including the SafeParse wrapper stored as a key, a Response treated as token data, the placeholder refresh token, and the zoho-bigin user id mix-up, are the kind that tests of the helpers' return values and the sync branch would catch. At minimum add tests for refreshOAuthTokens in both modes and for parseRefreshTokenResponse's return shape.

Refresh replaces the whole credential key with the raw refresh response

The stored key is overwritten with responseBody. In sync mode that response is the self-hoster's minimal payload (access token and expiry, per the comment in refreshOAuthTokens), so refresh_token and other stored fields are dropped from the credential. A later non-sync refresh then has no refresh token to use. The new fields should be merged into the existing key, as the Zoom and Google paths do.

Schema selection here does not match the sync condition used in refreshOAuthTokens

The minimal schema is selected when only the env vars are set. refreshOAuthTokens also requires a userId before calling the sync endpoint. So for team-owned credentials (userId null) on a sync-enabled instance, the provider's direct refresh response is validated with the minimal schema, which strips expires_in, expiry_date, refresh_token and instance_url. Google and Zoom then persist NaN or placeholder values. The schema choice should use the same condition as the branch that produced the response, or be passed in by the caller.

Sync request carries no authentication and its response is not status-checked

The outbound POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends only calcomUserId and appSlug, with no shared secret or signature, so the endpoint cannot verify that the request came from this instance. The reply is then trusted to overwrite stored tokens. There is no timeout and no response.ok check, so an error page or a stalled endpoint is handled as a token response. The inbound webhook already uses a shared secret, so the outbound call should send one too, with a timeout and a status check.

Zoom and Google route refreshed tokens through parseRefreshTokenResponse so the sync endpoint only needs to return an access token and expiry. Webex does not. This line validates against webexRefreshedTokenSchema, which requires an exact scope literal, token_type, refresh_token and refresh_token_expires_in. A sync endpoint following the documented contract (access token plus expiry) is always rejected with 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned'. Also, expiry_date is only updated when expires_in is present (lines 103-105), so an endpoint that returns only an expiry never updates it. Webex should use the same helper as Zoom.

Webhook credential update does not clear the invalid flag

When a provider returns invalid_grant, the code sets credential.invalid = true (googlecalendar, webex, zoom and invalidateCredential). This handler replaces the key with freshly synced tokens but never resets invalid. A credential flagged invalid therefore stays invalid after the self-hoster pushes working tokens, and any code path that skips invalid credentials keeps skipping it. The update should also set invalid to false.

Webhook secret is compared with !== instead of a constant-time comparison

The shared secret is compared with the !== operator, which short-circuits on the first mismatched character and can leak timing information about the secret. The route is the only authentication on an endpoint that writes decrypted third-party credentials, so use crypto.timingSafeEqual (hashing both sides first so lengths match).

Zoom refresh sends appSlug 'zoomvideo' but the credential is stored under appId 'zoom'

The Zoom callback creates credentials with appId 'zoom' (zoomvideo/api/callback.ts) and the installed-app path also uses slug 'zoom'. The sync request here sends appSlug 'zoomvideo', the directory name. A self-hoster's app store keyed by the Cal.com app slug will not find the app, or will find the wrong one, so Zoom sync refresh fails or returns the wrong credentials. The slug should match the stored appId.

Zoom sync-mode refresh computes expiry_date from a field the minimal schema strips

In sync mode parseRefreshTokenResponse validates with minimumTokenResponseSchema, which keeps only access_token, so expires_in is removed. newTokens.expires_in is therefore undefined, expiry_date becomes NaN, and it is persisted (serialized as null). The next getToken calls zoomTokenSchema.parse, which requires expiry_date to be a number, so the credential fails to parse and Zoom calls reject with 'Zoom credential keys parsing error' until the user reconnects.

The lookup (lines 62-70) and the create (line 83) are separate statements with no transaction or unique constraint covering (userId, appId). Two deliveries for the same user and app, such as a self-hoster retry, can both see no row and both insert. Later reads use findFirst and pick one row arbitrarily, so the app may keep using a stale token. The comment about upsert does not address this race. Wrap the lookup and write in a transaction, or enforce uniqueness at the database level.

isTokenValid is inverted, so expired tokens are never refreshed and valid ones always are

isTokenValid returns true when token.expiryDate < Date.now(), meaning the token is expired. getToken then does isTokenValid(...) ? resolve() : refreshAccessToken(...), so an expired token skips refresh and the stale access token is used, while a still-valid token triggers a refresh on every call. This is the path the PR wraps in refreshOAuthTokens. Also, line 219 stores expiryDate as Date.now() + 60 * 60, which is 3.6 seconds in milliseconds, so the stored expiry is wrong as well. The pre-existing defect is in code this PR modifies and should be fixed alongside it.

prisma is used in the Salesforce CalendarService but never imported

getClient now calls prisma.credential.update (line 96), but the file's imports (lines 1-20) do not include prisma from @calcom/prisma. This fails type-checking ('Cannot find name prisma') and throws a ReferenceError on every Salesforce connection, so the Salesforce calendar integration cannot be constructed.
